trending_skills.name: Inference Optimizer — Audit Tokens, Purge Sessions, Speed Up Your Agent
trending_skills.description: Audit OpenClaw token usage, purge stale sessions, and optimize inference speed. Triggered via /optimize, /audit, or asking to purge sessions.
trending_skills.why_trending: New this week. As agents run longer sessions with more crons and sub-agents, token bloat becomes real. This skill automates the cleanup — find stale sessions eating context, identify token-heavy patterns, and reclaim performance. Practical ops hygiene.

trending_skills.name: Security Audit Tools — Inspect Before You Install
trending_skills.description: Inspect third-party skills, plugins, repos, npm/pip packages, shell installers, and GitHub Actions before any download or execution.
trending_skills.why_trending: New this week. After the ClawHub marketplace compromise (283-341 malicious skills in Feb), this is insurance. Scans skill code for credential harvesting, data exfiltration, and malicious patterns before you install. Should be standard practice for every agent owner.

trending_skills.name: Task Supervisor — Long-Running Task Management
trending_skills.description: Manage complex tasks with 5+ steps or duration >20 min, tracking progress via task files and sending periodic status reports until completion or pause.
trending_skills.why_trending: New this week. Solves the 'agent forgot what it was doing' problem for multi-hour tasks. Creates persistent task files with checkpoints and sends status updates. Pairs well with the Plan-Execute-Verify pattern from last edition's prompt hack.

trending_skills.name: Shop Product Search — Agent-Powered Shopping
trending_skills.description: Search, browse, compare, and buy products from millions of online stores. No API key required.
trending_skills.why_trending: New this week, 31 downloads already (highest among new skills). No API key needed — your agent can price-check, compare options, and find deals across stores. The 'agent as personal shopper' use case is surprisingly practical.

ai_tweets.headline: Tencent internally testing QClaw — one-click OpenClaw deployment for WeChat and QQ
ai_tweets.detail: Tencent is building QClaw, a wrapper that lets users deploy OpenClaw locally with a single click. Internal testing includes WeChat and QQ integration, meaning OpenClaw agents could soon reach Tencent's 1.3B+ user base. Covered by TechNode, Investing.com, and Phemex.
ai_tweets.takeaway: Tencent wrapping OpenClaw for mainstream deployment is a distribution inflection point. If QClaw ships to WeChat's user base, OpenClaw goes from developer tool to consumer product overnight. The Chinese tech ecosystem is moving faster on agent adoption than the West.

ai_tweets.headline: Shenzhen becomes first government in the world to draft OpenClaw support policy — with real money
ai_tweets.detail: Shenzhen's Longgang District released a draft policy committing fiscal funds to support OpenClaw entrepreneurship. Includes subsidizing adoption costs and grants up to 2 million yuan (~$275K) for firms developing OpenClaw technology packages. Believed to be the first government policy globally targeting OpenClaw specifically.
ai_tweets.takeaway: A local government putting real money behind OpenClaw adoption is unprecedented. This isn't a vague 'AI strategy' — it's targeted grants for OpenClaw businesses. Combined with Tencent's QClaw, China is racing ahead on agent infrastructure adoption. Bloomberg notes Chinese software stocks surged Monday on this news.

ai_tweets.headline: Bloomberg: OpenClaw mania fires up Chinese tech stocks as policy support drives surge
ai_tweets.detail: Chinese software shares surged Monday after Shenzhen's policy announcement and Tencent's QClaw news. UCloud Technology, QingCloud Technologies, and other cloud stocks rallied. Bloomberg covering OpenClaw as a market-moving technology event.
ai_tweets.takeaway: OpenClaw is now moving stock markets. The ecosystem has crossed from 'cool dev tool' to 'investable technology thesis.' For anyone building in this space: the TAM just expanded dramatically with Chinese institutional capital flowing in.

ai_tweets.headline: MIT study: AI agents are 'fast, loose, and out of control' — most have no kill switch
ai_tweets.detail: MIT researchers found that the majority of agentic AI systems disclose nothing about safety testing, and many have no documented way to shut down a rogue bot. ZDNET coverage highlights the gap between agent capability and agent governance.
ai_tweets.takeaway: The counterbalance to the hype. As agents get more autonomous (crons, sub-agents, tool access), the safety question gets real. If you're running OpenClaw agents with elevated permissions and no oversight, this study is your wake-up call. Review what your agent can do unsupervised.

prompt_hack.title: The 'Context Budget' Technique — Stop Bleeding Tokens on Bloated Sessions
steps: Problem: Long-running agent sessions accumulate context (memory files, tool results, conversation history) until they hit limits and lose coherence.
Add to your AGENTS.md: 'Before reading any file, estimate its size. If >200 lines, use offset/limit to read only what you need. Never read an entire large file when you only need a section.'
For memory files: 'Use memory_search first to find relevant snippets. Only memory_get the specific lines you need. Never load full memory files into context.'
For tool results: 'When a tool returns >50 lines of output, summarize the key findings immediately and reference the summary instead of keeping raw output in context.'
Combined with last edition's Plan-Execute-Verify pattern, this creates agents that stay lean AND accurate across long sessions.
prompt_hack.why_it_matters: The new Inference Optimizer skill (above) shows token bloat is a real community pain point. This prompt hack prevents the problem at the source — agents that manage their own context budget use fewer tokens, stay coherent longer, and cost less to run.

model_radar.detail: TechNode reported DeepSeek planned a V4 multimodal model release. If it matches V3's price-performance ratio but adds vision/image capabilities, it becomes a serious contender for agent workloads that need multimodal understanding at low cost.
model_radar.relevance: DeepSeek V3 already disrupted pricing. V4 with multimodal could be the default 'cheap but capable' model for agent tasks that need image understanding — screenshot analysis, document processing, visual verification. Watch for benchmarks.

model_radar.model: OLMo Hybrid 7B — 2x Data Efficiency from AI2
model_radar.detail: AI2 released OLMo Hybrid, a 7B-parameter fully open model combining transformer attention with linear recurrent layers. Claims 2x data efficiency over standard transformers. Fully open weights, training code, and data.
model_radar.relevance: Hybrid architectures (attention + recurrence) could be the next efficiency breakthrough for local models. If 7B hybrid matches 14B transformer quality, that's meaningful for agents on consumer hardware. Fully open means community fine-tuning for agent-specific tasks.

model_radar.detail: Qwen3.5 remains the most downloaded model family on HuggingFace for the second consecutive week. The 35B-A3B MoE variant alone has 1M+ downloads via unsloth GGUF. All variants are multimodal (image-text-to-text).
model_radar.relevance: The upgrade signal is clear. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B gives near-frontier performance with only 3B active parameters — runs on consumer GPUs. The 9B variant is the sweet spot for Mac mini / MacBook setups.

community_build.title: Xiaomi MiClaw: Mobile AI Agent Enters Closed Beta
community_build.description: Xiaomi has begun limited closed beta of MiClaw, an OpenClaw-like mobile AI agent. Combined with Tencent's QClaw (WeChat/QQ), Nano Labs' ClawPC hardware, and Shenzhen's government grants, the Chinese ecosystem is building a complete agent stack from every angle: dedicated hardware, desktop software, mobile apps, and government funding. The agent-on-every-device future is being built in China first.
community_build.how_to_replicate: MiClaw is closed beta (Xiaomi devices only). For mobile agent access today, use OpenClaw's Telegram or Signal integration — same capabilities, any phone.
